title: The Algorithm Knows My Mother Better Than I Do
script: Aisyah: [unsettled] I found my mother's phone open to an advertisement so precisely tailored to her situation that I genuinely wondered, briefly, whether someone had been listening to our private conversations.
Rendra: [wry] Nobody needed to listen. The inference alone is damning enough without invoking anything so dramatic as surveillance.
Aisyah: [curious] Meaning what, exactly? She hasn't searched for anything remotely related.

Rendra: [explanatory] She didn't need to. Enough adjacent behavior, browsing patterns, the time she lingers on certain articles, the pauses before she scrolls past something, aggregates into a portrait more candid than most confessions.
Aisyah: [troubled] That's a considerably more intimate portrait than I'd feel comfortable handing a stranger, and yet she's handed it over without ever consciously agreeing to anything.
Rendra: [measured] Consent, in this context, is largely theatrical. Nobody reads the document; everybody clicks accept, and the theater satisfies a legal requirement rather than an ethical one.
Aisyah: [frustrated] So what would meaningful consent even look like, practically, for someone her age who barely trusts the device to begin with?

Rendra: [thoughtful] Probably something closer to a standing conversation than a one-time checkbox, revisited periodically as her circumstances shift, rather than buried in a document nobody was ever expected to read.
Aisyah: [skeptical] That sounds appealing in theory and entirely unprofitable in practice, which is presumably why no platform has volunteered for it.
Rendra: [dry] Precisely. The business model depends on exactly the opacity you're objecting to. Transparency and profitability are, in this particular arrangement, natural adversaries.
Aisyah: [resolute] Then I suppose the least I can do is sit with her and actually walk through what she's agreed to, badly translated legalese and all.
Rendra: [warmly] That's not nothing. An hour of genuine explanation probably does more good than any regulation currently pending.
Aisyah: [wry] Small comfort, given how thoroughly the algorithm's already finished its portrait of her.
Rendra: [gently] Finished portraits can still be corrected, Aisyah. That's rather the whole point of intervening now instead of never.
